title.zh: 卷一 本紀第一: 太祖
title.raw: 卷一 本紀第一: 太祖 Volume 1 Annals 1: Taizu

sentences.zh: 太祖法天啟運聖武皇帝，諱鐵木真，姓奇渥溫氏，蒙古部人。

translations.literal: Taizu, Emperor Conforming to Heaven, Initiating Fortune, Sacredly Martial — taboo name Temüjin, surname the Kiyad clan, a man of the Mongol tribe.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu, the Emperor Who Conformed to Heaven, Initiated Fortune, and Was Sacredly Martial, bore the personal name Temüjin; he belonged to the Kiyad clan and was a man of the Mongol tribe.

sentences.zh: 太祖其十世祖孛端義兒，母曰阿蘭果火，嫁脫奔咩哩犍，生二子，長曰博寒葛答黑，次曰博合睹撒裏直。

translations.literal: Taizu's tenth-generation ancestor was Boduanchid; his mother was called Alan Gua. She married Dobun Meren and bore two sons: the elder was Bo'arji, the younger Belgüdei.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu's tenth-generation ancestor was Boduanchid. His mother, Alan Gua, married Dobun Meren and bore two sons—the elder Bo'arji and the younger Belgüdei.

sentences.zh: 既而夫亡，阿蘭寡居，夜寢帳中，夢白光自天窗中入，化為金色神人，來趨臥榻。

translations.literal: Later her husband died; Alan lived as a widow. One night as she slept in her tent, she dreamed that a white light entered through the smoke-hole, transformed into a golden divine being, and came toward her couch.
translations.idiomatic: After her husband died, Alan lived alone as a widow. One night, asleep in her tent, she dreamed that a shaft of white light entered through the smoke-hole, became a golden divine figure, and moved toward her bed.

sentences.zh: 阿蘭驚覺，遂有娠，產一子，即孛端義兒也。

translations.literal: Alan awoke in alarm, then became pregnant and bore a son — Boduanchid.
translations.idiomatic: Startled awake, Alan soon found herself with child and gave birth to a son—Boduanchid.

sentences.zh: 孛端義兒狀貌奇異，沉默寡言，家人謂之癡，獨阿蘭語人曰：「此兒非癡，後世子孫必有大貴者。

translations.literal: Boduanchid's appearance was strange and he was silent and sparing of words; the household called him a simpleton. Only Alan told people: "This child is no simpleton; among later generations of his descendants there will surely be one of great eminence.
translations.idiomatic: Boduanchid looked odd and spoke little; the family took him for a fool. Alan alone told others, "This boy is no fool—among his descendants there will surely be someone of great eminence.

sentences.zh: 」阿蘭沒，諸兄分家貲，不及之。

translations.literal: " After Alan died, her elder brothers divided the family property and gave him nothing.
translations.idiomatic: " After Alan died, her elder brothers divided the family property and left him with nothing.

sentences.zh: 孛端義兒曰：「貧賤富貴，命也，貲財何足道！

translations.literal: Boduanchid said: "Poverty and wealth, low estate and high — these are fate; what are goods and wealth worth speaking of!
translations.idiomatic: Boduanchid said, "Poverty and wealth, low estate and high—these are fate. What are goods and wealth worth?

sentences.zh: 」獨乘青白馬，至八里屯阿懶之地居焉。

translations.literal: " He alone mounted a gray-white horse and went to dwell at Balitun Alan.
translations.idiomatic: " He mounted a gray-white horse alone and went to live at Balitun Alan.

sentences.zh: 食飲無所得，適有蒼鷹搏野獸而食，孛端義兒以緡設機取之，鷹即馴狎，乃臂鷹，獵兔禽以為膳，或闕即繼，似有天相之。

translations.literal: For food and drink he had nothing; just then a dark eagle was striking wild beasts to eat. Boduanchid set a snare with cord and took it; the eagle at once grew tame, so he put it on his arm and hunted rabbits and birds for his meals. Whenever one was lacking, another followed—as though Heaven favored him.
translations.idiomatic: He had nothing to eat or drink. Then he saw a dark eagle strike down a wild beast to feed. Boduanchid snared it with a cord; the bird grew tame at once. He kept it on his arm and hunted rabbits and fowl for his meals—and whenever one quarry failed, another seemed to appear, as if Heaven were watching over him.

sentences.zh: 居月，有民數十家自統急裏忽魯之野逐水草來遷。

translations.literal: After a month, several dozen households of people came migrating from the pastures of Tongjilihur, following grass and water.
translations.idiomatic: After a month, several dozen households arrived from the pastures of Tongjilihur, moving with the grass and water.

sentences.zh: 孛端義兒結茅與之居，出入相資，自此生理稍足。

translations.literal: Boduanchid built huts and lived with them; going out and coming in they supported one another, and from this his livelihood gradually became sufficient.
translations.idiomatic: Boduanchid built huts and settled among them; they helped one another in daily life, and from then on his livelihood slowly improved.

sentences.zh: 一日，仲兄忽思之，曰：「孛端義兒獨出而無齎，近者得無凍餒乎？

translations.literal: One day his second elder brother thought of him and said: "Boduanchid went out alone without provisions; those nearby—could he not be freezing and starving?
translations.idiomatic: One day his second elder brother thought of him and said, "Boduanchid went off alone without provisions—could he not be freezing and starving by now?

sentences.zh: 」即自來訪，邀與俱歸。

translations.literal: " He came himself to visit and invited him to return together.
translations.idiomatic: " He came to visit in person and invited Boduanchid to return home with him.

sentences.zh: 孛端義兒中路謂其兄曰：「統急裏忽魯之民無所屬附，若臨之以兵，可服也。

translations.literal: Midway Boduanchid said to his brother: "The people of Tongjilihur have no one to attach themselves to; if we come upon them with troops, they can be made to submit.
translations.idiomatic: On the way Boduanchid told his brother, "The people of Tongjilihur have no lord to follow. If we confront them with armed men, they can be brought to submit.

sentences.zh: 」兄以為然，至家，即選壯士，令孛端義兒帥之前行，果盡降之。

translations.literal: " The brother agreed; upon reaching home he at once selected strong men and ordered Boduanchid to lead them forward — and indeed they all surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: " His brother agreed. When they reached home, he chose strong men at once and sent Boduanchid ahead in command—and indeed the people all submitted.

sentences.zh: 孛端義兒歿，子八林昔黑剌禿合必畜嗣，生子曰咩撚篤敦。

translations.literal: Boduanchid died; his son Ba'arji Borjigidai succeeded him and begot a son named Menen Tudun.
translations.idiomatic: When Boduanchid died, his son Ba'arji Borjigidai succeeded him and fathered a son named Menen Tudun.

sentences.zh: 咩撚篤敦妻曰莫拿倫，生七子而寡。

translations.literal: Menen Tudun's wife was called Monolun; she bore seven sons and became a widow.
translations.idiomatic: Menen Tudun's wife was Monolun. She bore seven sons and was widowed.

sentences.zh: 莫拿倫性剛急。

translations.literal: Monolun's nature was fierce and impatient.
translations.idiomatic: Monolun was fierce and hot-tempered by nature.

sentences.zh: 時押剌伊而部有群小兒掘田間草根以為食，莫拿倫乘車出，適見之，怒曰：「此田乃我子馳馬之所，群兒輒敢壞之邪？

translations.literal: At that time in the Yamagha Er tribe a band of small children were digging field roots for food. Monolun drove out in her cart and happened to see them. Angry, she said: "This field is where my sons ride their horses — how dare you children ruin it!
translations.idiomatic: At that time, children of the Yamagha Er tribe were digging roots in the fields for food. Monolun drove out in her cart and saw them. In anger she cried, "This field is where my sons ride their horses—how dare you children ruin it!

sentences.zh: 」驅車徑出，輾傷諸兒，有至死者。

translations.literal: " She drove straight through and ran over the children; some were killed.
translations.idiomatic: " She drove straight through and ran over the children, killing some of them.

sentences.zh: 押剌伊而忿怨，盡驅莫拿倫馬群以去。

translations.literal: Yamagha Er, filled with resentment, drove off all of Monolun's herds of horses.
translations.idiomatic: Burning with resentment, the Yamagha Er drove off every horse in Monolun's herds.

sentences.zh: 莫拿倫諸子聞之，不及被甲，往追之。

translations.literal: Monolun's sons, hearing of it, went in pursuit without time to don armor.
translations.idiomatic: When Monolun's sons heard what had happened, they set out in pursuit without stopping to put on armor.

sentences.zh: 莫拿倫私憂曰：「吾兒不甲以往，恐不能勝敵。

translations.literal: Monolun privately worried and said: "My sons go without armor; I fear they cannot overcome the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Monolun worried privately and said, "My sons are going without armor—I fear they cannot defeat the enemy.

sentences.zh: 」令子婦載甲赴之，已無及矣。

translations.literal: " She ordered her daughters-in-law to load armor and go after them, but it was already too late.
translations.idiomatic: " She sent her daughters-in-law after them with armor, but it was already too late.

sentences.zh: 既而果為所敗，六子皆死。

translations.literal: Presently they were indeed defeated; six sons all died.
translations.idiomatic: They were indeed defeated; all six sons were killed.

sentences.zh: 押剌伊而乘勝殺莫拿倫，滅其家。

translations.literal: Yamagha Er pressed the victory, killed Monolun, and destroyed her household.
translations.idiomatic: Yamagha Er pressed their advantage, killed Monolun, and wiped out her household.

sentences.zh: 唯一長孫海都尚幼，乳母匿諸積木中，得免。

translations.literal: Only one eldest grandson, Qaidu, was still young; his nurse hid him among stacked firewood and he escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Only the eldest grandson, Qaidu, was still a child. His nurse hid him in a stack of firewood, and he survived.

sentences.zh: 先是莫拿倫第七子納真，於八剌忽民家為贅婿，故不及難。

translations.literal: Earlier Monolun's seventh son Nachin had become a live-in son-in-law in a Barughu household, and so did not suffer the calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Monolun's seventh son, Nachin, had earlier married into a Barughu family and so was spared the disaster.

sentences.zh: 聞其家被禍，來視之，見病嫗十數與海都尚在，其計無所出，幸驅馬時，兄之黃馬三次掣套竿逸歸，納真至是得乘之。

translations.literal: Hearing that his family had met disaster, he came to look; he saw a dozen or so sick old women and Qaidu still alive. He had no plan — but by good fortune, when the horses were driven off, his elder brother's yellow horse three times broke its halter pole and ran back; Nachin was thus able to ride it.
translations.idiomatic: When he heard that disaster had struck his family, he came to see. A dozen or so sick old women and young Qaidu were still alive, but he could think of no way forward. By good fortune, when the horses were driven off, his elder brother's yellow horse had three times broken its halter pole and run back—and Nachin was now able to ride it.

sentences.zh: 乃偽為牧馬者，詣押剌伊而。

translations.literal: He then disguised himself as a horse-herder and went to Yamagha Er.
translations.idiomatic: He disguised himself as a horse-herder and went to Yamagha Er.

sentences.zh: 路逢父子二騎先後行，臂鷹而獵。

translations.literal: On the road he met a father and son riding one after another, falcons on their arms, out hunting.
translations.idiomatic: On the road he met a father and son riding one behind the other, falcons on their arms, out hunting.

sentences.zh: 納真識其鷹，曰：「此吾兄所擎者也。

translations.literal: Nachin recognized their falcons and said: "These are the ones my elder brother carried.
translations.idiomatic: Nachin recognized their falcons and said, "Those are the birds my elder brother used to carry.

sentences.zh: 」趨前紿其少者曰：「有赤馬引群馬而東，汝見之乎？

translations.literal: " He hurried forward and deceived the younger man: "A red horse is leading a herd eastward — have you seen it?
translations.idiomatic: " He hurried forward and deceived the younger man. "A red horse is leading a herd eastward—have you seen it?

translations.literal: He said: "No.
translations.idiomatic: The younger man said, "No.

sentences.zh: 」少者乃問曰：「爾所經過有鳧雁乎？

translations.literal: " The younger man then asked: "On the way you came, were there wild ducks and geese?
translations.idiomatic: " Then the younger man asked, "On the way you came, were there wild ducks and geese?

translations.literal: He said: "There were.
translations.idiomatic: Nachin said, "There were.

sentences.zh: 」曰：「汝可為吾前導乎？

translations.literal: " He said: "Can you guide us ahead?
translations.idiomatic: " The younger man said, "Will you guide us ahead?

translations.literal: He said: "I can.
translations.idiomatic: Nachin said, "I can.

sentences.zh: 」遂同行。

translations.literal: " They then traveled together.
translations.idiomatic: " They traveled on together.

sentences.zh: 轉一河隈，度後騎相去稍遠，刺殺之。

translations.literal: Turning a bend of the river, once the rear rider was somewhat farther off, he stabbed and killed the younger man.
translations.idiomatic: At a bend in the river, once the rider behind had fallen a little farther back, he stabbed the younger man and killed him.

sentences.zh: 縶馬與鷹，趨迎後騎，紿之如初。

translations.literal: He tied up the horse and falcon, hurried to meet the rear rider, and deceived him as before.
translations.idiomatic: He secured the horse and falcon, rode forward to meet the man behind, and deceived him in the same way.

sentences.zh: 後騎問曰：「前射鳧雁者，吾子也，何為久臥不起耶？

translations.literal: The rear rider asked: "The one ahead who was shooting wild ducks and geese — that was my son; why does he lie so long and not rise?
translations.idiomatic: The rear rider asked, "The man ahead who was shooting ducks and geese—that was my son. Why is he lying there so long and not getting up?

sentences.zh: 」納真以鼻衄對。

translations.literal: Nachin answered that he had a nosebleed.
translations.idiomatic: Nachin said he had a nosebleed.

sentences.zh: 騎者方怒，納真乘隙刺殺之。

translations.literal: As the rider was about to grow angry, Nachin seized the opening and stabbed and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Just as the rider was about to fly into a rage, Nachin seized the moment and stabbed him to death.

sentences.zh: 復前行，至一山下，有馬數百，牧者唯童子數人，方擊髀石為戲。

translations.literal: He went on again and came to a mountain foot where there were several hundred horses; the herders were only a few boys, striking hip bones in play.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed on to the foot of a mountain, where several hundred horses were grazing. Only a few boys were tending them, playing a game of striking hip bones.

sentences.zh: 納真熟視之，亦兄家物也。

translations.literal: Nachin looked closely — they too were from his elder brother's household.
translations.idiomatic: Nachin looked closely and saw that these too belonged to his elder brother's household.

sentences.zh: 紿問童子，亦如之。

translations.literal: He deceived and questioned the boys, and they answered the same way.
translations.idiomatic: He questioned the boys with the same ruse, and they answered as before.

sentences.zh: 於是登山四顧，悄無來人，盡殺童子，驅馬臂鷹而還，取海都並病嫗，歸八剌忽之地止焉。

translations.literal: Thereupon he climbed the mountain, looked around on all sides — no one was coming — killed all the boys, drove off the horses with falcons on his arm, and returned; he took Qaidu and the sick old women and stopped at Barughu.
translations.idiomatic: He climbed the hill and looked around—no one was coming. He killed all the boys, drove off the horses with a falcon on his arm, and returned. He gathered Qaidu and the sick old women and settled at Barughu.

sentences.zh: 海都稍長，納真率八剌忽怯谷諸民，共立為君。

translations.literal: When Qaidu had grown somewhat, Nachin led the people of Barughu and the Qiegu valley and together set him up as lord.
translations.idiomatic: When Qaidu had grown a little older, Nachin led the people of Barughu and the Qiegu valley and together made him their lord.

sentences.zh: 海都既立，以兵攻押剌伊而，臣屬之，形勢浸大，列營帳於八剌合黑河上，跨河為梁，以便往來。

translations.literal: Once Qaidu was established, he attacked Yamagha Er with troops, made them his subjects, and his power gradually grew great. He set up camp tents on the Balqabuqin River and built a bridge across the river to ease coming and going.
translations.idiomatic: Once Qaidu was established, he attacked Yamagha Er with an army, brought them under his rule, and his power steadily grew. He pitched camp along the Balqabuqin River and built a bridge across it for easier travel.

sentences.zh: 由是四傍部族歸之者漸眾。

translations.literal: From this the tribes roundabout who submitted to him gradually became numerous.
translations.idiomatic: From then on, more and more neighboring tribes came over to him.

sentences.zh: 海都歿，子拜姓忽兒嗣。

translations.literal: Qaidu died; his son Bayan Qul succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: When Qaidu died, his son Bayan Qul succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 拜姓忽兒歿，子敦必乃嗣。

translations.literal: Bayan Qul died; his son Dombinü succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: When Bayan Qul died, his son Dombinü succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 敦必乃歿，子葛不律寒嗣。

translations.literal: Dombinü died; his son Khabul succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: When Dombinü died, his son Khabul succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 葛不律寒歿，子八哩丹嗣。

translations.literal: Khabul died; his son Bartan succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: When Khabul died, his son Bartan succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 八哩丹歿，子也速該嗣，併吞諸部落，勢愈盛大。

translations.literal: Bartan died; his son Yesügei succeeded, annexed the various tribes, and his power became still more vast.
translations.idiomatic: When Bartan died, his son Yesügei succeeded him, absorbed the surrounding tribes, and his power grew still greater.

sentences.zh: 也速該崩，至元三年十月，追諡烈祖神元皇帝。

translations.literal: Yesügei died; in the tenth month of the third year of Zhiyuan he was posthumously given the temple name Liezu and the title Emperor Shenyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Yesügei died. In the tenth month of the third year of the Zhiyuan reign, he was posthumously honored as Liezu, the Divine Origin Emperor.

sentences.zh: 初，烈祖征塔塔兒部，獲其部長鐵木真。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Liezu campaigned against the Tatar tribe, he captured their chieftain Temüjin.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Liezu campaigned against the Tatar tribe, he captured their chieftain Temüjin.

sentences.zh: 宣懿太后月倫適生帝，手握凝血如赤石。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Xuanyi, Hö'elün, had just given birth to the Emperor; in his hand was congealed blood like a red stone.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Xuanyi, Hö'elün, had just given birth to the Emperor; clutched in his fist was congealed blood like a red stone.

sentences.zh: 烈祖異之，因以所獲鐵木真名之，志武功也。

translations.literal: Liezu marveled at it and therefore named him after the Temüjin he had captured, to record martial achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Liezu took this as a marvel and named the child after the Temüjin he had captured, to mark a deed of arms.

sentences.zh: 族人泰赤烏部舊與烈祖相善，後因塔兒不台用事，遂生嫌隙，絕不與通。

translations.literal: Among the clansmen, the Taichi'ut tribe had long been on good terms with Liezu; later, because Targhutai came to power, they came to bear resentment and broke off all contact.
translations.idiomatic: Among the clansmen, the Taichi'ut had long been on good terms with Liezu, but after Targhutai rose to power they turned hostile and cut off all contact.

sentences.zh: 及烈祖崩，帝方幼沖，部眾多歸泰赤烏。

translations.literal: When Liezu died, the Emperor was still young; many of the tribesmen went over to the Taichi'ut.
translations.idiomatic: When Liezu died, the Emperor was still very young, and many tribesmen went over to the Taichi'ut.

sentences.zh: 近侍有脫端火兒真者，亦將叛，帝自泣留之。

translations.literal: Among those close at hand was Toghoril, who also intended to rebel; the Emperor wept and himself detained him.
translations.idiomatic: Among those close at hand was Toghoril, who also meant to rebel. The Emperor wept and begged him to stay.

sentences.zh: 脫端曰：「深池已幹矣，堅石已碎矣，留復何為！

translations.literal: Toghoril said: "The deep pool has already dried; the hard stone has already shattered — what is the use of staying!
translations.idiomatic: Toghoril said, "The deep pool has already dried up, the hard stone has already shattered—what good is there in staying?

sentences.zh: 」竟帥眾馳去。

translations.literal: " In the end he led his followers and galloped away.
translations.idiomatic: " In the end he led his followers away at a gallop.

sentences.zh: 宣懿太后怒其弱己也，麾旗將兵，躬自追叛者，驅其太半而還。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Xuanyi, angry that he had slighted her, waved the banner and led troops, personally pursuing the deserters, and drove back more than half of them.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Xuanyi, furious that he had slighted her, took up the banner, led troops in person after the deserters, and drove more than half of them back.

sentences.zh: 時帝麾下搠只別居薩里河。

translations.literal: At that time Shigi, among those under the Emperor's command, was separately encamped on the Sali River.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Shigi, one of the Emperor's commanders, was encamped separately on the Sali River.

sentences.zh: 劄木合部人禿台察兒居玉律哥泉，時欲相侵淩，掠薩里河牧馬以去。

translations.literal: Toqto'a of the Jamuqa tribe was encamped at Yulige Spring; he then intended mutual encroachment and raided the Sali River horse herds and drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: Toqto'a of Jamuqa's tribe was camped at Yulige Spring and now meant to encroach on neighboring grounds; he raided the horse herds on the Sali River and drove them away.

sentences.zh: 搠只麾左右匿群馬中，射殺之。

translations.literal: Shigi waved his attendants to hide among the horse herds and shot and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Shigi signaled his men to hide among the herds and shot Toqto'a dead.

sentences.zh: 劄木合以為怨，遂與泰赤烏諸部合謀，以眾三萬來戰。

translations.literal: Jamuqa took this as a grievance and therefore joined in conspiracy with the Taichi'ut tribes, coming to battle with thirty thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Jamuqa nursed this as a grievance and joined the Taichi'ut tribes in a plot, marching to battle with thirty thousand men.

sentences.zh: 帝時駐軍答蘭版硃思之野，聞變，大集諸部兵，分十有三翼以俟。

translations.literal: The Emperor was then encamped on the plain of Dalann Banshi; hearing of the uprising, he greatly gathered troops from the tribes, divided into thirteen wings, and waited.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was then encamped on the plain of Dalann Banshi. When he heard of the revolt, he mustered troops from the tribes in force, arrayed them in thirteen wings, and waited.

sentences.zh: 已而劄木合至，帝與大戰，破走之。

translations.literal: Presently Jamuqa arrived; the Emperor fought a great battle with him and routed him.
translations.idiomatic: When Jamuqa arrived, the Emperor fought him in a great battle and put him to rout.

sentences.zh: 當是時，諸部之中，唯泰赤烏地廣民眾，號為最強。

translations.literal: At that time, among the tribes, only the Taichi'ut lands were broad and their people numerous; they were called the strongest.
translations.idiomatic: At that time, among all the tribes, only the Taichi'ut held broad lands and a large population—they were reckoned the strongest.

sentences.zh: 其族照烈部，與帝所居相近。

translations.literal: Among their clans, the Khori Chin tribe lived close to where the Emperor dwelt.
translations.idiomatic: Among their clans, the Khori Chin lived near the Emperor's camp.

sentences.zh: 帝常出獵，偶與照烈獵騎相屬。

translations.literal: The Emperor often went out hunting and once happened to have hunting riders in succession with the Khori Chin.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor often went hunting and once happened to ride in succession with Khori Chin hunters.

sentences.zh: 帝謂之曰：「今夕可同宿乎？

translations.literal: The Emperor said to them: "Tonight may we lodge together?
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said to them, "Shall we camp together tonight?

sentences.zh: 」照烈曰：「同宿固所願，但從者四百，因糗糧不具，已遣半還矣，今將奈何？

translations.literal: Khori Chin said: "Lodging together is indeed our wish, but our followers are four hundred; because provisions were not ready, we have already sent half back — what are we to do now?
translations.idiomatic: The Khori Chin replied, "We would gladly camp together, but we have four hundred followers. Our provisions were not ready, so we have already sent half of them back—what can we do now?

sentences.zh: 」帝固邀與宿，凡其留者，悉飲食之。

translations.literal: The Emperor firmly invited them to lodge; all who remained he fully fed and watered.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor insisted that they stay, and fed and watered every man who remained.

sentences.zh: 明日再合圍，帝使左右驅獸向照烈，照烈得多獲以歸。

translations.literal: The next day they joined the hunt again; the Emperor had his attendants drive game toward the Khori Chin, and the Khori Chin returned with much taken.
translations.idiomatic: The next day they hunted together again. The Emperor had his men drive game toward the Khori Chin, and they returned with a rich catch.

sentences.zh: 其眾感之，私相語曰：「泰赤烏與我雖兄弟，常攘我車馬，奪我飲食，無人君之度。

translations.literal: Their people were moved and privately said to one another: "The Taichi'ut, though brothers to us, constantly seize our carts and horses and take our food and drink — they have no measure of a lord.
translations.idiomatic: His men were deeply moved and whispered among themselves, "The Taichi'ut are our kinsmen, yet they constantly seize our carts and horses and take our food—they have no lord's measure.

sentences.zh: 有人君之度者，其惟鐵木真太子乎？

translations.literal: One who has a lord's measure — is it not Temüjin, the Prince?
translations.idiomatic: A man who has a lord's measure—could that not be Prince Temüjin?

sentences.zh: 」照烈之長玉律，時為泰赤烏所虐，不能堪，遂與塔海答魯領所部來歸，將殺泰赤烏以自效。

translations.literal: Yurki, elder of the Khori Chin, was then being abused by the Taichi'ut and could not endure it; he therefore came over with Tajghir leading their tribe to submit, intending to kill the Taichi'ut to prove his loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Yurki, chief of the Khori Chin, was then being mistreated by the Taichi'ut and could bear it no longer. He came over with Tajghir at the head of their tribe, intending to kill the Taichi'ut to prove his loyalty.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「我方熟寐，幸汝覺我，自今車轍人跡之途，當盡奪以與汝矣。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "I was just sleeping soundly; fortunately you woke me. From now on, every road of wheel tracks and human footprints — I shall seize them all and give them to you.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "I was sleeping soundly—you did well to wake me. From now on, every road marked by wheel tracks and footprints shall be taken from others and given to you.

sentences.zh: 」已而二人不能踐其言，復叛去。

translations.literal: Presently the two could not carry out their word and rebelled and went away again.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the two men failed to keep their word and rebelled and left again.

sentences.zh: 塔海答魯至中路，為泰赤烏部人所殺，照烈部遂亡。

translations.literal: Tajghir, midway on the road, was killed by men of the Taichi'ut tribe; the Khori Chin tribe was thus destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Midway on the road Tajghir was killed by men of the Taichi'ut tribe, and the Khori Chin tribe was destroyed.

sentences.zh: 時帝功德日盛，泰赤烏諸部多苦其主非法，見帝寬仁，時賜人以裘馬，心悅之。

translations.literal: At that time the Emperor's merit and virtue daily grew; many of the Taichi'ut tribes suffered under their lords' lawlessness. Seeing the Emperor's lenience and generosity, and that he often bestowed furs and horses on men, they were pleased in heart.
translations.idiomatic: By then the Emperor's reputation was rising daily. Many Taichi'ut tribes suffered under lawless chiefs; when they saw his lenience and generosity, and how often he gave men furs and horses, their hearts went out to him.

sentences.zh: 若赤老溫、若哲別、若失力哥也不幹諸人，若朵郎吉、若劄剌兒、若忙兀諸部，皆慕義來降。

translations.literal: Such men as Chilaun, Jebe, and Shilgen; such tribes as Dojinkai, Jelme, and the Mangqut — all admired his righteousness and came to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Men such as Chilaun, Jebe, and Shilgen, and tribes such as Dojinkai, Jelme, and the Mangqut—all came over in admiration of his righteousness.

sentences.zh: 帝會諸族薛徹、大醜等，各以旄車載湩酪，宴於斡難河上。

translations.literal: The Emperor assembled the clans Shechü, Taiju, and others; each brought kumiss and fermented mare's milk in banner-decked carts and feasted on the Onon River.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor gathered the clans—Shechü, Taiju, and others—each bringing kumiss and fermented mare's milk in carts hung with banners, and they feasted on the Onon River.

sentences.zh: 帝與諸族及薛徹別吉之毋忽兒真之前，共置馬湩一革囊；

translations.literal: Before Quljin, mother of Shechü Beji, and before the Emperor and the clans, they jointly set out one leather bag of mare's milk;
translations.idiomatic: Before Quljin, mother of Shechü Beji, and before the Emperor and the assembled clans, they together set out one leather bag of mare's milk;

sentences.zh: 薛徹別吉次毋野別該之前，獨置一革囊。

translations.literal: before Yebügei, younger sister of Shechü Beji, they alone set out one leather bag.
translations.idiomatic: before Yebügei, younger sister of Shechü Beji, they set out a leather bag by themselves.

sentences.zh: 忽兒真怒曰：「今不尊我，而貴野別該乎？

translations.literal: Quljin angrily said: "Today you do not honor me, yet you honor Yebügei?
translations.idiomatic: Quljin said angrily, "Today you do not honor me, yet you honor Yebügei?

sentences.zh: 」疑帝之主膳者失丘兒所為，遂笞之。

translations.literal: " Suspecting that Shikhur, the Emperor's master of provisions, had done this, she had him beaten with rods.
translations.idiomatic: " Suspecting that Shikhur, the Emperor's master of provisions, was responsible, she had him beaten with rods.

sentences.zh: 於是頗有隙。

translations.literal: From this there was considerable estrangement.
translations.idiomatic: From this a serious rift opened between them.

sentences.zh: 時皇弟別裏古台掌帝乞列思事，乞列思，華言禁外系馬所也。

translations.literal: At that time the Emperor's younger brother Belgütei managed the qiliesi affairs; qiliesi, in the Chinese language, is the place outside the forbidden precinct where horses are tethered.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Emperor's younger brother Belgütei managed the qiliesi—the tethering ground outside the camp where horses were hitched, as the Chinese term has it.

sentences.zh: 播裏掌薛徹別吉乞列思事。

translations.literal: Bori managed the qiliesi affairs of Shechü Beji.
translations.idiomatic: Bori managed the qiliesi for Shechü Beji.

sentences.zh: 播裏從者因盜去馬靷，別裏古台執之。

translations.literal: Bori's followers stole away horse reins; Belgütei seized them.
translations.idiomatic: Followers of Bori stole away horse reins, and Belgütei seized them.

sentences.zh: 播裏怒，斫別裏古台，傷其背。

translations.literal: Bori grew angry and hacked at Belgütei, wounding his back.
translations.idiomatic: Bori flew into a rage and struck Belgütei with a blade, wounding his back.

sentences.zh: 左右欲鬥，別裏古台止之，曰：「汝等欲即復仇乎？

translations.literal: Those at hand wished to fight; Belgütei stopped them and said: "Do you wish to take revenge at once?
translations.idiomatic: Those around them wanted to fight, but Belgütei stopped them and said, "Do you mean to take revenge at once?

sentences.zh: 我傷幸未甚，姑待之。

translations.literal: My wound is fortunately not severe; for the moment let us wait.
translations.idiomatic: My wound is fortunately not serious—for now, let us wait.

sentences.zh: 」不聽，各持馬乳橦疾鬥，奪忽兒真、火裏真二哈敦以歸。

translations.literal: They would not listen; each took up a mare's-milk cudgel and fought swiftly, seizing the two queens Quljin and Huljin and returning.
translations.idiomatic: They would not listen. Each seized a mare's-milk cudgel and fought at once, then carried off the two queens Quljin and Huljin and returned.

sentences.zh: 薛徹別吉遣使請和，因令二哈敦還。

translations.literal: Kököchü sent envoys to sue for peace and therefore had the two khadun returned.
translations.idiomatic: Kököchü sent envoys to sue for peace and had the two wives sent back.

sentences.zh: 會塔塔兒部長蔑兀真笑裏徒背金約，金主遣丞相完顏襄帥兵逐之北走。

translations.literal: It happened that Megujin Seüle, chieftain of the Tatar tribe, broke the Jin covenant; the Jin ruler sent the chief minister Wanyan Xiang at the head of troops to drive him fleeing north.
translations.idiomatic: About then Megujin Seüle, chieftain of the Tatar tribe, broke his treaty with the Jin. The Jin emperor sent Chief Minister Wanyan Xiang with an army to drive him north in flight.

sentences.zh: 帝聞之，發近兵自斡難河迎擊，仍諭薛徹別吉帥部人來助。

translations.literal: The Emperor heard of it, mobilized nearby troops from the Onon River to meet and strike, and still instructed Kököchü to lead his tribesmen to assist.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor heard of this, he mobilized nearby troops from the Onon River to intercept the enemy and ordered Kököchü to bring his tribesmen to help.

sentences.zh: 候六日不至，帝自與戰，殺蔑兀真笑裏徒，盡虜其輜重。

translations.literal: He waited six days and they did not arrive; the Emperor fought by himself, killed Megujin Seüle, and captured all their baggage train.
translations.idiomatic: After waiting six days with no sign of them, the Emperor fought alone, killed Megujin Seüle, and captured the entire baggage train.

sentences.zh: 帝之麾下有為乃蠻部人所掠者，帝欲討之，復遣六十人徵兵於薛徹別吉。

translations.literal: Among those under the Emperor's command were men who had been plundered by people of the Naiman tribe; the Emperor wished to punish them and again sent sixty men to levy troops from Kököchü.
translations.idiomatic: Some of the Emperor's followers had been plundered by Naiman tribesmen. Intent on punishing them, he sent sixty men to Kököchü to demand troops.

sentences.zh: 薛徹別吉以舊怨之故，殺其十人，去五十人衣而歸之。

translations.literal: Kököchü, because of old grievances, killed ten of them, stripped the fifty of their clothing, and sent them back.
translations.idiomatic: Nursing old grievances, Kököchü killed ten of the envoys, stripped the other fifty of their clothes, and sent them back.

sentences.zh: 帝怒曰：「薛徹別吉曩笞我失丘兒，斫傷我別裏古台，今又敢乘敵勢以陵我耶？

translations.literal: The Emperor said in anger: "Kököchü once flogged my Shigiuchu and hacked my Belgutei; now he dares again, taking advantage of the enemy's strength, to treat me with contempt?
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said in anger, "Kököchü once flogged my man Shigiuchu and wounded my Belgutei—and now he dares, while the enemy still presses, to treat me with contempt?

sentences.zh: 」因帥兵逾沙磧攻之，殺虜其部眾，唯薛徹、大醜僅以妻孥免。

translations.literal: " He therefore led troops across the sandy wastes to attack them, killed and captured their tribesmen, and only Kököchü and Daichu escaped with wives and children.
translations.idiomatic: " He led troops across the sandy wastes to attack them, killed and captured their tribesmen, and only Kököchü and Daichu escaped with their wives and children.

sentences.zh: 越數月，帝復伐薛徹、大醜，追至帖烈徒之隘，滅之。

translations.literal: After several months the Emperor again campaigned against Kököchü and Daichu, pursued them to the pass of Telütu, and destroyed them.
translations.idiomatic: Several months later the Emperor marched again against Kököchü and Daichu, pursued them to the Telütu Pass, and destroyed them.

sentences.zh: 克烈部劄阿紺孛來歸。

translations.literal: Jaqa Gambu of the Kerait tribe came over in submission.
translations.idiomatic: Jaqa Gambu of the Kerait tribe came over to submit.

sentences.zh: 劄阿紺孛者，部長汪罕之弟也。

translations.literal: Jaqa Gambu was the younger brother of the chieftain Ong Khan.
translations.idiomatic: Jaqa Gambu was the younger brother of the chieftain Ong Khan.

sentences.zh: 汪罕名脫裏，受金封爵為王，番言音重，故稱王為汪罕。

translations.literal: Ong Khan's name was Toghrul; he received a Jin enfeoffment as king — in the barbarian tongue the word for king is heavily accented, so he was called Ong Khan.
translations.idiomatic: Ong Khan's personal name was Toghrul. The Jin had enfeoffed him as king; in the barbarian tongue the word for king is heavily accented, so he was called Ong Khan.

sentences.zh: 初，汪罕之父忽兒劄胡思杯祿既卒，汪罕嗣位，多殺戮昆弟。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Ong Khan's father Qurjaqus Buyruq had died, Ong Khan succeeded to the chieftainship and killed many of his brothers.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, after Ong Khan's father Qurjaqus Buyruq died, Ong Khan succeeded as chieftain and put many of his brothers to death.

sentences.zh: 其叔父菊兒罕帥兵與汪罕戰，逼於哈剌溫隘，敗之，僅以百餘騎脫走，奔於烈祖。

translations.literal: His uncle Gur Khan led troops to fight Ong Khan, pressed him at the Kharun Pass, defeated him, and he escaped with only a little over a hundred horsemen and fled to Liezu.
translations.idiomatic: His uncle Gur Khan led troops against Ong Khan, cornered him at Kharun Pass, and routed him. Ong Khan escaped with barely a hundred horsemen and fled to Liezu.

sentences.zh: 烈祖親將兵逐菊兒罕走西夏，復奪部眾歸汪罕。

translations.literal: Liezu personally led troops in pursuit, driving Gur Khan to flee toward the Western Xia, and recovered the tribesmen and restored them to Ong Khan.
translations.idiomatic: Liezu led troops in person, drove Gur Khan toward the Western Xia, recovered the tribesmen, and restored them to Ong Khan.

sentences.zh: 汪罕德之，遂相與盟，稱為按答。

translations.literal: Ong Khan was grateful for this and therefore entered alliance with him, calling each other anda.
translations.idiomatic: Ong Khan was deeply grateful and entered into alliance with him, each calling the other anda.

sentences.zh: 按答，華言交物之友也。

translations.literal: Anda, in the Chinese language, is a friend who exchanges gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Anda, in Chinese usage, means a sworn friend who exchanges gifts.

sentences.zh: 烈祖崩，汪罕之弟也力可哈剌，怨汪罕多殺之故，復叛歸乃蠻部。

translations.literal: When Liezu died, Ong Khan's younger brother Elqa Qara, resenting Ong Khan's many killings, rebelled again and returned to the Naiman tribe.
translations.idiomatic: After Liezu died, Ong Khan's younger brother Elqa Qara, resentful of Ong Khan's many killings, rebelled again and went over to the Naiman.

sentences.zh: 乃蠻部長亦難赤為發兵伐汪罕，盡奪其部眾與之。

translations.literal: Inanch Bilge, chieftain of the Naiman tribe, raised troops to attack Ong Khan, seized all his tribesmen, and gave them to Elqa Qara.
translations.idiomatic: Inanch Bilge, chieftain of the Naiman tribe, raised troops against Ong Khan, seized all his followers, and handed them over to Elqa Qara.

sentences.zh: 汪罕走河西、回鶻、回回三國，奔契丹。

translations.literal: Ong Khan fled through the three lands of Hexi, the Uighurs, and the Muslims, and took refuge with the Khitan.
translations.idiomatic: Ong Khan fled through Hexi, the Uighur lands, and the Muslim territories, and took refuge with the Khitan.

sentences.zh: 既而復叛歸，中道糧絕，捋羊乳為飲，刺橐駝血為食，困乏之甚。

translations.literal: Before long he rebelled and returned; midway his provisions ran out — he milked ewes for drink and pierced camels for blood as food; his exhaustion was extreme.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he rebelled and turned back. On the road his provisions gave out; he drank ewe's milk and pierced camels for blood to eat, and was brought to the edge of collapse.

sentences.zh: 帝以其與烈祖交好，遣近侍往招之。

translations.literal: Because he had been on friendly terms with Liezu, the Emperor sent close attendants to summon him.
translations.idiomatic: Because Ong Khan had been on friendly terms with Liezu, the Emperor sent close attendants to summon him.

sentences.zh: 帝親迎撫勞，安置軍中振給之，遂會於土兀剌河上，尊汪罕為父。

translations.literal: The Emperor personally went out to welcome and comfort him, settled him in the army and supplied his needs, then met with him on the Tuul River and honored Ong Khan as father.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor went out in person to welcome and comfort him, settled him in camp and supplied his needs, then met him on the Tuul River and honored Ong Khan as a father.

sentences.zh: 未幾，帝伐蔑裏乞部，與其部長脫脫戰於莫那察山，遂掠其資財、田禾，以遺汪罕。

translations.literal: Before long the Emperor campaigned against the Merkit tribe, fought their chieftain Toqto'a on Mount Monach, and then plundered their goods, wealth, and grain fields and presented them to Ong Khan.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Emperor marched against the Merkit, fought their chieftain Toqto'a on Mount Monach, plundered their goods, wealth, and grain fields, and sent the spoils to Ong Khan.

sentences.zh: 汪罕因此部眾稍集。

translations.literal: Because of this Ong Khan's tribesmen gradually gathered again.
translations.idiomatic: Because of this Ong Khan's followers gradually gathered again.

sentences.zh: 居亡何，汪罕自以其勢足以有為，不告於帝，獨率兵復攻蔑裏乞部。

translations.literal: After not long, Ong Khan, thinking his own strength sufficient for action, without informing the Emperor, alone led troops to attack the Merkit tribe again.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Ong Khan, believing his strength sufficient for great deeds, attacked the Merkit again on his own without telling the Emperor.

sentences.zh: 部人敗走，脫脫奔八兒忽真之隘。

translations.literal: The tribesmen were defeated and fled; Toqto'a fled to the pass of Barghuchin.
translations.idiomatic: The Merkit were defeated and fled; Toqto'a escaped to the Barghuchin Pass.

sentences.zh: 汪罕大掠而還，於帝一無所遺，帝不以屑意。

translations.literal: Ong Khan plundered heavily and returned, giving the Emperor nothing at all; the Emperor did not regard it as worth minding.
translations.idiomatic: Ong Khan looted heavily and returned, giving the Emperor nothing at all—and the Emperor did not think it worth troubling over.

sentences.zh: 會乃蠻部長不欲魯罕不服，帝復與汪罕征之。

translations.literal: It happened that Buyiru Khan, chieftain of the Naiman tribe, was insubordinate; the Emperor again campaigned against him together with Ong Khan.
translations.idiomatic: Buyiru Khan, chieftain of the Naiman tribe, had grown insubordinate, and the Emperor again marched against him together with Ong Khan.

sentences.zh: 至黑辛八石之野，遇其前鋒也的脫孛魯者，領百騎來戰，見軍勢漸逼，走據高山，其馬鞍轉墜，擒之。

translations.literal: Reaching the plain of Kökseengge, they encountered their vanguard Yedi Tügelü leading a hundred horsemen to battle; seeing the army's strength pressing closer, he fled and took the high mountain — his saddle turned and he fell; they captured him.
translations.idiomatic: Reaching the plain of Kökseengge, they met the Naiman vanguard under Yedi Tügelü, who came out with a hundred horsemen to fight. Seeing the enemy pressing in, he fled to the heights; his saddle turned and he fell, and they took him captive.

sentences.zh: 曾未幾何，帝復與乃蠻驍將曲薛吾撒八剌二人遇，會日暮，各還營壘，約明日戰。

translations.literal: Before long the Emperor again encountered the two Naiman fierce generals Qusqa and Sabra; as dusk fell each returned to camp and agreed to fight the next day.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Emperor again encountered the two Naiman fierce generals Qusqa and Sabra. Dusk fell, each side returned to camp, and they agreed to fight the next day.

sentences.zh: 是夜，汪罕多燃火營中，示人不疑，潛移部眾於別所。

translations.literal: That night Ong Khan lit many fires in camp to show he suspected nothing, and secretly moved his tribesmen elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: That night Ong Khan lit many fires in camp to show he suspected nothing, while secretly moving his tribesmen elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 及旦，帝始知之，因頗疑其有異志，退師薩里河。

translations.literal: At dawn the Emperor first learned of it; he therefore grew quite suspicious of disloyal intent and withdrew the army to the Sali River.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn the Emperor learned of it and grew deeply suspicious of disloyal intent; he withdrew the army to the Sali River.

sentences.zh: 既而汪罕亦還至土兀剌河，汪罕子亦剌合及劄阿紺孛來會。

translations.literal: Presently Ong Khan also returned to the Tuul River; Ong Khan's son Ilugei and Jaqa Gambu came to join him.
translations.idiomatic: Presently Ong Khan also returned to the Tuul River, where his son Ilugei and Jaqa Gambu came to join him.

sentences.zh: 曲薛吾等察知之，乘其不備，襲虜其部眾於道。

translations.literal: Qusqa and the others observed and learned of this; taking them unawares, they raided and captured their tribesmen on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Qusqa and his men learned of this and, catching them unawares, raided and captured Ong Khan's followers on the road.

sentences.zh: 亦剌合奔告汪罕，汪罕命亦剌合與卜魯忽共追之，且遣使來曰：「乃蠻不道，掠我人民，太子有四良將，能假我以雪恥乎？

translations.literal: Ilugei ran to tell Ong Khan; Ong Khan ordered Ilugei and Burulgu together to pursue them, and also sent envoys saying: "The Naiman are lawless — they have plundered our people. The Prince has four fine generals; will you lend them to me to wipe away this shame?
translations.idiomatic: Ilugei ran to tell Ong Khan. Ong Khan ordered Ilugei and Burulgu to pursue together and sent envoys saying, "The Naiman are lawless—they have plundered our people. The Prince has four fine generals; will you lend them to me so I may wipe away this shame?

sentences.zh: 」帝頓釋前憾，遂遣博爾術、木華黎、博羅渾、赤老溫四人，帥師以往。

translations.literal: " The Emperor at once set aside former grievances and therefore sent Bo'orchu, Muqali, Borokhula, and Chilaun — four men — to lead troops there.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor at once set aside former grievances and sent Bo'orchu, Muqali, Borokhula, and Chilaun at the head of troops.

sentences.zh: 師未至，亦剌合已追及曲薛吾，與之戰，大敗，卜魯忽成擒，流矢中亦剌合馬胯，幾為所獲。

translations.literal: The army had not yet arrived when Ilugei had already overtaken Qusqa and fought him, suffering a great defeat; Burulgu was captured, a stray arrow struck Ilugei's horse's crupper, and he was nearly taken.
translations.idiomatic: Before the army arrived, Ilugei had already overtaken Qusqa and fought him, only to suffer a great defeat. Burulgu was captured, a stray arrow struck Ilugei's horse in the crupper, and Ilugei was nearly taken.

sentences.zh: 須臾，四將至，擊乃蠻走，盡奪所掠歸汪罕。

translations.literal: In a moment the four generals arrived, struck the Naiman and put them to flight, and fully recovered what had been plundered and returned it to Ong Khan.
translations.idiomatic: In a moment the four generals arrived, routed the Naiman, recovered everything that had been plundered, and returned it to Ong Khan.

sentences.zh: 已而與皇弟哈撒兒再伐乃蠻，拒鬥於忽蘭盞側山，大敗之，盡殺其諸將族眾，積屍以為京觀，乃蠻之勢遂弱。

translations.literal: Presently, together with the imperial younger brother Hasar, he again campaigned against the Naiman; they fought them off at the side of Mount Qulanjan, routed them greatly, killed all their generals and clansmen, piled corpses to make a barrow, and the Naiman power was thereby weakened.
translations.idiomatic: Presently, together with his imperial younger brother Hasar, he campaigned against the Naiman again. They fought them off at the foot of Mount Qulanjan, routed them utterly, killed their generals and clansmen, and piled the corpses into a barrow—the Naiman power was broken from that day.

sentences.zh: 時泰赤烏猶強，帝會汪罕於薩里河，與泰赤烏部長沆忽等大戰斡難河上，敗走之，斬獲無算。

translations.literal: At that time the Taichi'ut were still strong; the Emperor joined Ong Khan on the Sali River and fought a great battle with the Taichi'ut chieftain Hangha and others on the Onon River, routed and put them to flight, and killed and captured beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: The Taichi'ut were still strong. The Emperor joined Ong Khan on the Sali River and fought a great battle with the Taichi'ut chieftain Hangha and others on the Onon River, routed them, and killed and captured beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 哈答斤部、散只兀部、朵魯班部、塔塔兒部、弘吉剌部聞乃蠻、泰赤烏敗，皆畏威不自安，會於阿雷泉，斬白馬為誓，欲襲帝及汪罕。

translations.literal: The Qadaghin tribe, the Saji'ut tribe, the Dorben tribe, the Tatar tribe, and the Hongirad tribe — hearing of the Naiman and Taichi'ut defeats — all feared the power and were ill at ease; they met at Alai Spring, slaughtered a white horse in oath, and intended to strike the Emperor and Ong Khan.
translations.idiomatic: The Qadaghin, Saji'ut, Dorben, Tatar, and Hongirad tribes, hearing of the defeats of the Naiman and Taichi'ut, all feared the power arrayed against them and could not rest easy. They met at Alai Spring, slaughtered a white horse in oath, and plotted to strike the Emperor and Ong Khan.

sentences.zh: 弘吉剌部長迭夷恐事不成，潛遣人告變。

translations.literal: Döyin, chieftain of the Hongirad tribe, feared the affair would not succeed and secretly sent a man to report the plot.
translations.idiomatic: Döyin, chieftain of the Hongirad tribe, feared the plot would fail and secretly sent a man to report it.

sentences.zh: 帝與汪罕自虎圖澤逆戰於杯亦烈川，又大敗之。

translations.literal: The Emperor and Ong Khan, from Hutuge, met them in battle on the Bei'ilie River and again routed them greatly.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor and Ong Khan marched from Hutuge to meet them on the Bei'ilie River and routed them again.

sentences.zh: 汪罕遂分兵，自由怯綠憐河而行。

translations.literal: Ong Khan then divided his troops and went by way of the Qorqonaq River on his own.
translations.idiomatic: Ong Khan then divided his forces and marched separately by way of the Qorqonaq River.

sentences.zh: 劄阿紺孛謀於按敦阿述、燕火脫兒等曰：「我兄性行不常，既屠絕我昆弟，我輩又豈得獨全乎？

translations.literal: Jaqa Gambu plotted with Altan Achi, Yamun Toor, and others, saying: "My elder brother's conduct is inconstant; having already slaughtered all our brothers, how can we alone remain whole?
translations.idiomatic: Jaqa Gambu plotted with Altan Achi, Yamun Toor, and others, saying, "My elder brother's conduct is inconstant. Having already slaughtered all our brothers, how can we alone remain safe?

sentences.zh: 」按敦阿述泄其言，汪罕令執燕火脫兒等至帳下，解其縛，且謂燕火脫兒曰：「吾輩由西夏而來，道路饑困，其相誓之語，遽忘之乎？

translations.literal: " Altan Achi leaked their words; Ong Khan ordered Yamun Toor and the others seized and brought before his tent, released their bonds, and said to Yamun Toor: "We came from the Western Xia — on the road we were hungry and exhausted; have you already forgotten the words of our mutual oath?
translations.idiomatic: " Altan Achi leaked their words. Ong Khan had Yamun Toor and the others seized and brought before his tent, released their bonds, and said to Yamun Toor, "We came from the Western Xia—on the road we were hungry and exhausted. Have you already forgotten the words of our mutual oath?

sentences.zh: 」因唾其面，坐上之人皆起而唾之。

translations.literal: " He therefore spat in his face, and all those seated rose and spat at him.
translations.idiomatic: " He spat in his face, and all those seated rose and spat at him as well.

sentences.zh: 汪罕又屢責劄阿紺孛，至於不能堪，劄阿紺孛與燕火脫兒等俱奔乃蠻。

translations.literal: Ong Khan again repeatedly reproached Jaqa Gambu until he could not bear it; Jaqa Gambu, together with Yamun Toor and the others, all fled to the Naiman.
translations.idiomatic: Ong Khan again and again reproached Jaqa Gambu until he could bear it no longer. Jaqa Gambu fled to the Naiman together with Yamun Toor and the others.

sentences.zh: 帝駐軍於徹徹兒山，起兵伐塔塔兒部。

translations.literal: The Emperor encamped at Mount Chechir and raised troops to campaign against the Tatar tribe.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor encamped at Mount Chechir and raised troops to campaign against the Tatar tribe.

sentences.zh: 部長阿剌兀都兒等來逆戰，大敗之。

translations.literal: The chieftain Alaq Usun and others came to meet them in battle; he routed them greatly.
translations.idiomatic: The chieftain Alaq Usun and others came out to meet them in battle, and he routed them.

sentences.zh: 時弘吉剌部欲來附，哈撒兒不知其意，往掠之。

translations.literal: At that time the Hongirad tribe wished to come over in submission; Hasar did not know their intent and went to plunder them.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Hongirad wished to come over in submission, but Hasar did not know their intent and went to plunder them.

sentences.zh: 於是弘吉剌歸劄木合部，與朵魯班、亦乞剌思、哈答斤、火魯剌思、塔塔兒、散只兀諸部，會於犍河，共立劄木合為局兒罕，盟於禿律別兒河岸，為誓曰：「凡我同盟，有泄此謀者，如岸之摧，如林之伐。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Hongirad returned to Jamuqa's tribe; together with the Dorben, Yiqilas, Qadaghin, Qorulas, Tatar, and Saji'ut tribes they met on the Qian River, jointly set up Jamuqa as Gur Khan, allied on the bank of the Tölü Bayir River, and swore an oath saying: "All who are of our alliance — if any reveal this plot, may he be like a bank crumbling, like a forest felled.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the Hongirad returned to Jamuqa's tribe. Together with the Dorben, Yiqilas, Qadaghin, Qorulas, Tatar, and Saji'ut tribes they met on the Qian River, set Jamuqa up as Gur Khan, and on the bank of the Tölü Bayir River swore an oath: "All who are of our alliance—if any reveal this plot, may he crumble like a bank and fall like a forest felled.

sentences.zh: 」誓畢，共舉足蹋岸，揮刀斫林，驅士卒來侵。

translations.literal: " When the oath was finished, together they stamped the bank with their feet, waved blades and hacked at the forest, and drove their soldiers to invade.
translations.idiomatic: " When the oath was finished, they stamped the bank with their feet, hacked at the forest with their blades, and drove their soldiers to invade.

sentences.zh: 塔海哈時在眾中，與帝麾下抄吾兒連姻。

translations.literal: Taqaiqa was then among the assembly; he was connected by marriage with Cha'ur under the Emperor's command.
translations.idiomatic: Taqaiqa was then among the assembly; he was connected by marriage with Cha'ur, one of the Emperor's followers.

sentences.zh: 抄吾兒偶往視之，具知其謀，即還至帝所，悉以其謀告之。

translations.literal: Cha'ur happened to go to visit him, fully learned their plot, and at once returned to the Emperor's place and told him the whole plot.
translations.idiomatic: Cha'ur happened to visit him, learned the whole plot, returned at once to the Emperor, and told him everything.

sentences.zh: 帝即起兵，逆戰於海剌兒、帖尼火魯罕之地，破之，劄木合脫走，弘吉剌部來降。

translations.literal: The Emperor immediately raised troops and met them in battle at the place of Qailar and Tengi Qorqan, broke them, Jamuqa escaped, and the Hongirad tribe came to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor immediately raised troops and met them in battle at Qailar and Tengi Qorqan, broke them, and Jamuqa escaped while the Hongirad came over in surrender.

sentences.zh: 歲壬戌，帝發兵於兀魯回失連真河，伐按赤塔塔兒、察罕塔塔兒二部。

translations.literal: In the year renchen the Emperor mobilized troops on the Ülüi Qutuqan River and campaigned against the Aq Tatar and Qa'an Tatar tribes.
translations.idiomatic: In the renchen year the Emperor mobilized troops on the Ülüi Qutuqan River and campaigned against the Aq Tatar and Qa'an Tatar tribes.

sentences.zh: 先誓師曰：「苟破敵逐北，見棄遺物，慎無獲，俟軍事畢散之。

translations.literal: First he addressed the army in oath, saying: "If we break the enemy and pursue them north, and you see abandoned goods — take care not to seize them; wait until the military affair is finished and then divide them.
translations.idiomatic: First he addressed the army in oath, saying, "If we break the enemy and pursue them north, and you see abandoned goods—take care not to seize them. Wait until the campaign is finished and then divide the spoils.

sentences.zh: 」既而果勝，族人按彈、火察兒、答力台三人背約，帝怒，盡奪其所獲，分之軍中。

translations.literal: " Presently they indeed won; clansmen Altan, Quchar, and Targhutai — three men — broke the covenant; the Emperor was angry and fully seized what they had taken and divided it among the army.
translations.idiomatic: " They won as he had foretold. Three clansmen—Altan, Quchar, and Targhutai—broke the covenant. The Emperor was angry, seized everything they had taken, and divided it among the army.

sentences.zh: 初，脫脫敗走八兒忽真隘，既而復出為患，帝帥兵討走之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Toqto'a had been defeated and fled to the Barghuchin Pass; before long he came out again and made trouble; the Emperor led troops to campaign against him and drive him off.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Toqto'a had been defeated and fled to the Barghuchin Pass; before long he came out again and made trouble, and the Emperor led troops to drive him off.

sentences.zh: 至是又會乃蠻部不欲魯罕約朵魯班、塔塔兒、哈答斤、散只兀諸部來侵。

translations.literal: At this time Buyiru Khan of the Naiman tribe again joined with the Dorben, Tatar, Qadaghin, and Saji'ut tribes to come and invade.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Buyiru Khan of the Naiman tribe again joined the Dorben, Tatar, Qadaghin, and Saji'ut tribes in an invasion.

sentences.zh: 帝遣騎乘高四望，知乃蠻兵漸至，帝與汪罕移軍入塞。

translations.literal: The Emperor sent horsemen up high places to look in the four directions, learned that Naiman troops were gradually arriving, and the Emperor and Ong Khan moved the army into the pass.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor sent horsemen to high ground to look in all directions, learned that Naiman troops were gradually arriving, and he and Ong Khan moved the army into the pass.

sentences.zh: 亦剌合自北邊來據高山結營，乃蠻軍沖之不動，遂還。

translations.literal: Ilugei came from the northern border, took the high mountain, and established camp; the Naiman army charged them but could not move them, and therefore returned.
translations.idiomatic: Ilugei came from the northern border, took the high ground, and established camp. The Naiman army charged but could not move him, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 亦剌合尋亦入塞。

translations.literal: Before long Ilugei also entered the pass.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Ilugei also entered the pass.

sentences.zh: 將戰，帝遷輜重於他所，與汪罕倚阿蘭塞為壁，大戰於闕奕壇之野，乃蠻使神巫祭風雪，欲因其勢進攻。

translations.literal: About to give battle, the Emperor moved the baggage train elsewhere; together with Ong Khan he relied on the Alan Pass as a wall and fought a great battle on the plain of Quyilan; the Naiman had a shaman sacrifice to wind and snow, wishing to advance the attack by that force.
translations.idiomatic: As battle drew near, the Emperor moved the baggage train elsewhere. Together with Ong Khan he took the Alan Pass as his wall and fought a great battle on the plain of Quyilan. The Naiman had a shaman sacrifice wind and snow, hoping to advance the attack by that force.

sentences.zh: 既而反風，逆擊其陣，乃蠻軍不能戰，欲引還。

translations.literal: Presently the wind reversed; he struck against their formation in reverse, and the Naiman army could not fight and wished to withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: Presently the wind reversed. He struck against their formation with the wind at his back, and the Naiman army could not hold and wished to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 雪滿溝澗，帝勒兵乘之，乃蠻大敗。

translations.literal: Snow filled the gullies and ravines; the Emperor restrained the army and pressed the advantage, and the Naiman were routed greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Snow filled the gullies and ravines. The Emperor held his army firm and pressed the advantage, and the Naiman were routed.

sentences.zh: 是時劄木合部起兵援乃蠻，見其敗，即還，道經諸部之立己者，大縱掠而去。

translations.literal: At this time Jamuqa's tribe raised troops to aid the Naiman; seeing their defeat, they at once returned, and passing through the tribes that had set him up, they plundered heavily and went away.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Jamuqa's tribe raised troops to aid the Naiman, but seeing their defeat they turned back at once and, passing through the tribes that had set him up as Gur Khan, plundered them heavily and went away.

sentences.zh: 帝欲為長子朮赤求昏於汪罕女抄兒伯姬，汪罕之孫禿撒合亦欲尚帝女火阿真伯姬，俱不諧，自是頗有違言。

translations.literal: The Emperor wished to seek marriage for his eldest son Jochi with Ong Khan's daughter Cha'er Beki; Ong Khan's grandson Toghusa also wished to marry the Emperor's daughter Ho'aqan Beki — neither came to agreement, and from this there were considerable words of estrangement.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor wished to seek marriage for his eldest son Jochi with Ong Khan's daughter Cha'er Beki; Ong Khan's grandson Toghusa also wished to marry the Emperor's daughter Ho'aqan Beki. Neither match came off, and from this bitter words began to pass between them.

sentences.zh: 初，帝與汪罕合軍攻乃蠻，約明日戰，劄木合言於汪罕曰：「我於君是白翎雀，他人是鴻雁耳。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the Emperor and Ong Khan joined armies to attack the Naiman and agreed to fight the next day, Jamuqa said to Ong Khan: "I to you am the white lark — others are wild geese.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when the Emperor and Ong Khan joined armies to attack the Naiman and agreed to fight the next day, Jamuqa said to Ong Khan, "I to you am the white lark—others are wild geese.

sentences.zh: 白翎雀寒暑常在北方，鴻雁遇寒則南飛就暖耳。

translations.literal: The white lark in cold and heat always stays in the north; wild geese, meeting cold, fly south to seek warmth.
translations.idiomatic: The white lark in cold and heat always stays in the north; wild geese, when cold comes, fly south to seek warmth.

sentences.zh: 」意謂帝心不可保也。

translations.literal: " The meaning was that the Emperor's heart could not be trusted.
translations.idiomatic: " He meant that the Emperor's loyalty could not be trusted.

sentences.zh: 汪罕聞之疑，遂移部眾於別所。

translations.literal: Ong Khan heard this and grew suspicious; he therefore moved his tribesmen elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: Ong Khan heard this and grew suspicious; he moved his tribesmen elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 及議昏不成，劄木合復乘隙謂亦剌合曰：「太子雖言是汪罕之子，嘗通信於乃蠻，將不利於君父子。

translations.literal: When the marriage negotiations failed, Jamuqa again seized the opening and said to Ilugei: "Though the Prince says he is Ong Khan's son, he has communicated with the Naiman and will bring harm upon you, father and son.
translations.idiomatic: When the marriage negotiations failed, Jamuqa again seized the opening and said to Ilugei, "Though the Prince calls himself Ong Khan's son, he has communicated with the Naiman and will bring harm upon you, father and son.

sentences.zh: 君若能加兵，我當從傍助君也。

translations.literal: If you can add troops, I will from the side assist you.
translations.idiomatic: If you will add troops, I will assist you from the flank.

sentences.zh: 」亦剌合信之。

translations.literal: " Ilugei believed him.
translations.idiomatic: " Ilugei believed him.

sentences.zh: 會答力台、火察兒、按彈等叛歸亦剌合，亦說之曰：「我等願佐君討宣懿太后諸子也。

translations.literal: It happened that Targhutai, Quchar, Altan, and others rebelled and returned to Ilugei; they also urged him, saying: "We wish to assist you in attacking the sons of Empress Dowager Xuanyi.
translations.idiomatic: It happened that Targhutai, Quchar, Altan, and others rebelled and returned to Ilugei. They also urged him, saying, "We wish to assist you in attacking the sons of Empress Dowager Xuanyi.

sentences.zh: 」亦剌合大喜，遣使言於汪罕。

translations.literal: " Ilugei was greatly pleased and sent envoys to speak to Ong Khan.
translations.idiomatic: " Ilugei was greatly pleased and sent envoys to speak to Ong Khan.

sentences.zh: 汪罕曰：「劄木合，巧言寡信人也，不足聽。

translations.literal: Ong Khan said: "Jamuqa is a man of clever words and little trust — not worth listening to.
translations.idiomatic: Ong Khan said, "Jamuqa is a man of clever words and little trust—not worth listening to.

sentences.zh: 」亦剌合力言之，使者往返者數四。

translations.literal: " Ilugei forcefully spoke his case; envoys went back and forth four times.
translations.idiomatic: " Ilugei pressed his case hard, and envoys went back and forth four times.

sentences.zh: 汪罕曰：「吾身之存，實太子是賴。

translations.literal: Ong Khan said: "That my body still lives is truly owing to the Prince.
translations.idiomatic: Ong Khan said, "That I still live is truly owing to the Prince.

sentences.zh: 髭須已白，遺骸冀得安寢，汝乃喋喋不已耶？

translations.literal: My beard and whiskers are already white; I hope my remains may rest in peace — yet you chatter on without end?
translations.idiomatic: My beard and whiskers are already white; I hope my bones may rest in peace—yet you chatter on without end?

sentences.zh: 汝善自為之，毋貽吾憂可也。

translations.literal: Do as you will — only do not bring me worry.
translations.idiomatic: Do as you will—only do not bring me worry.

sentences.zh: 」劄木合遂縱火焚帝牧地而去。

translations.literal: " Jamuqa therefore set fire to the Emperor's pasturelands and went away.
translations.idiomatic: " Jamuqa therefore set fire to the Emperor's pasturelands and went away.

sentences.zh: 歲癸亥，汪罕父子謀欲害帝，乃遣使者來曰：「向者所議姻事，今當相從，請來飲布渾察兒。

translations.literal: In the year guihai, Ong Khan, father and son, plotted to harm the Emperor; they therefore sent envoys saying: "The marriage matter discussed earlier — now we should follow through; please come and drink the betrothal wine.
translations.idiomatic: In the guihai year Ong Khan, father and son, plotted to harm the Emperor. They sent envoys saying, "The marriage we discussed earlier—we should now follow through. Please come and drink the betrothal wine.

sentences.zh: 」布渾察兒，華言許親酒也。

translations.literal: " Betrothal wine, in the Chinese language, is the wine of betrothal agreement.
translations.idiomatic: " Betrothal wine, in Chinese usage, is the wine drunk to seal a betrothal agreement.

sentences.zh: 帝以為然，率十騎赴之，至中道，心有所疑，命一騎往謝，帝遂還。

translations.literal: The Emperor thought it so, led ten horsemen to go; midway his heart grew suspicious, ordered one horseman to go and decline, and the Emperor then returned.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor believed them and set out with ten horsemen. Midway his heart grew suspicious; he ordered one horseman to go and decline, and turned back.

sentences.zh: 汪罕謀既不成，即議舉兵來侵。

translations.literal: Ong Khan's plot having failed, he at once deliberated raising troops to invade.
translations.idiomatic: When Ong Khan's plot failed, he at once resolved to raise troops and invade.

sentences.zh: 圉人乞失力聞其事，密與弟把帶告帝。

translations.literal: The groom Kishilik heard of the affair and secretly told the Emperor together with his younger brother Badai.
translations.idiomatic: The groom Kishilik heard of the affair and secretly told the Emperor together with his younger brother Badai.

sentences.zh: 帝即馳軍阿蘭塞，悉移輜重於他所，遣折裏麥為前鋒，俟汪罕至，即整兵出戰。

translations.literal: The Emperor immediately galloped the army to the Alan Pass, fully moved the baggage train elsewhere, sent Jebe as vanguard, and when Ong Khan arrived, at once arrayed troops and gave battle.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor immediately galloped the army to the Alan Pass, moved the baggage train elsewhere, sent Jebe as vanguard, and when Ong Khan arrived arrayed his troops and gave battle.

sentences.zh: 先與硃力斤部遇，次與董哀部遇，又次與火力失烈門部遇，皆敗之；

translations.literal: First he met the Jürkin tribe; next he met the Dong'ai tribe; again next he met the Qulijisimin tribe — all were routed;
translations.idiomatic: First he met the Jürkin tribe and routed them; next the Dong'ai tribe and routed them; then the Qulijisimin tribe and routed them as well;

sentences.zh: 最後與汪罕親兵遇，又敗之。

translations.literal: last he met Ong Khan's personal troops and again routed them.
translations.idiomatic: last he met Ong Khan's personal troops and routed them again.

sentences.zh: 亦剌合見勢急，突來沖陣，射之中頰，即斂兵而退。

translations.literal: Ilugei, seeing the situation urgent, suddenly came charging the formation; an arrow struck him in the cheek — he at once drew in his troops and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Ilugei, seeing the situation urgent, suddenly charged the formation; an arrow struck him in the cheek, and he at once drew in his troops and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 怯裏亦部人遂棄汪罕來降。

translations.literal: People of the Kerait tribe therefore abandoned Ong Khan and came to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Kerait tribesmen therefore abandoned Ong Khan and came over in surrender.

sentences.zh: 汪罕既敗而歸，帝亦將兵還，至董哥澤駐軍，遣阿里海致責於汪罕曰：「君為叔父菊兒罕所逐，困迫來歸，我父即攻菊兒罕，敗之於河西，其土地人民盡收與君，此大有功於君一也。

translations.literal: Ong Khan having been defeated returned; the Emperor also led troops back, encamped at Dongge Lake, and sent Ariq to deliver a rebuke to Ong Khan, saying: "You were driven off by your uncle Gur Khan, came back in distress and submitted — my father then attacked Gur Khan, defeated him west of the river, and all his lands and people were recovered and given to you: this was a great service to you, the first.
translations.idiomatic: Ong Khan, defeated, returned home. The Emperor also led his troops back, encamped at Dongge Lake, and sent Ariq to rebuke Ong Khan, saying, "You were driven off by your uncle Gur Khan and came back in distress to submit. My father attacked Gur Khan, defeated him west of the river, and recovered all his lands and people for you—this was the first great service done you.

sentences.zh: 君為乃蠻所攻，西奔日沒處。

translations.literal: You were attacked by the Naiman and fled west to where the sun sets.
translations.idiomatic: You were attacked by the Naiman and fled west to where the sun sets.

sentences.zh: 君弟劄阿紺孛在金境，我亟遣人召還。

translations.literal: Your younger brother Jaqa Gambu was in Jin territory; I urgently sent men to summon him back.
translations.idiomatic: Your younger brother Jaqa Gambu was in Jin territory, and I urgently sent men to summon him back.

sentences.zh: 比至，又為蔑裏乞部人所逼，我請我兄薛徹別及及我弟大醜往殺之，此大有功於君二也。

translations.literal: When he arrived, he was again pressed by people of the Merkit tribe; I asked my elder brother Kököchü and my younger brother Daichu to go and kill them — this was a great service to you, the second.
translations.idiomatic: When he arrived, Merkit tribesmen pressed him again. I asked my elder brother Kököchü and my younger brother Daichu to go and kill them—this was the second great service done you.

sentences.zh: 君困迫來歸時，我過哈丁裏，曆掠諸部羊、馬、資財，盡以奉君，不半月間，令君饑者飽，瘠者肥，此大有功於君三也。

translations.literal: When you came back in distress and submitted, I passed through Qatun and plundered sheep, horses, and goods from the various tribes, giving all to you; within half a month I made the hungry full and the lean fat — this was a great service to you, the third.
translations.idiomatic: When you came back in distress and submitted, I passed through Qatun, plundered sheep, horses, and goods from the surrounding tribes, and gave everything to you. Within half a month I made the hungry full and the lean fat—this was the third great service done you.

sentences.zh: 君不告我，往掠蔑裏乞部，大獲而還，未嘗以毫髮分我，我不以為意。

translations.literal: You did not tell me, but went to raid the Merkit tribe, returned with great gains, and never shared so much as a hair's breadth with me — I did not regard it as worth minding.
translations.idiomatic: You did not tell me, but went to raid the Merkit and returned with great gains, never sharing so much as a hair's breadth with me—I did not regard it as worth minding.

sentences.zh: 及君為乃蠻所傾覆，我遣四將奪還爾民人，重立爾國家，此大有功於君四也。

translations.literal: When you were overthrown by the Naiman, I sent four generals to recover your people, re-establish your state — this was a great service to you, the fourth.
translations.idiomatic: When the Naiman overthrew you, I sent four generals to recover your people and re-establish your state—this was the fourth great service done you.

sentences.zh: 我征朵魯班、塔塔兒、哈答斤、散只兀、弘吉剌五部，如海東鷙禽之於鵝雁，見無不獲，獲則必致於君，此大有功於君五也。

translations.literal: I campaigned against the Dorben, Tatar, Qadaghin, Saji'ut, and Hongirad — five tribes — like a fierce sea-eagle upon geese and wild swans: what I saw I took, and what I took I always sent to you — this was a great service to you, the fifth.
translations.idiomatic: I campaigned against the Dorben, Tatar, Qadaghin, Saji'ut, and Hongirad—five tribes—like a fierce sea-eagle upon geese and wild swans: what I saw I took, and what I took I always sent to you. This was the fifth great service done you.

sentences.zh: 是五者皆有明驗，君不報我則已，今乃易恩為仇，而遽加兵於我哉？

translations.literal: These five all have clear proof; if you would not repay me, so be it — yet now you turn kindness into enmity and suddenly send troops against me?
translations.idiomatic: These five deeds all stand proven. If you would not repay me, so be it—yet now you turn kindness into enmity and suddenly send troops against me?

sentences.zh: 」汪罕聞之，語亦剌合曰：「我向者之言何如？

translations.literal: " When Ong Khan heard this, he said to Ilugei: "Were my words of old not so?
translations.idiomatic: " When Ong Khan heard this, he said to Ilugei, "Were my words of old not so?

sentences.zh: 吾兒宜識之。

translations.literal: My son, you should mark them well.
translations.idiomatic: My son, you should mark them well.

sentences.zh: 」亦剌合曰：「事勢至今日，必不可已，唯有竭力戰鬥。

translations.literal: " Ilugei said: "The situation has come to this day — it cannot be stopped; there is nothing to do but fight with all our strength.
translations.idiomatic: " Ilugei said, "Matters have come to this pass—they cannot be stopped. There is nothing to do but fight with all our strength.

sentences.zh: 我勝則並彼，彼勝則並我耳。

translations.literal: If we win, we absorb them; if they win, they absorb us — that is all.
translations.idiomatic: If we win, we absorb them; if they win, they absorb us—that is all.

sentences.zh: 多言何為？

translations.literal: What is the use of many words?
translations.idiomatic: What is the use of many words?

sentences.zh: 」時帝諸族按彈、火察兒皆在汪罕左右，帝因遣阿里海誚責汪罕，就令告之曰：「昔者吾國無主，以薛徹、太醜二人實我伯祖八剌哈之裔，欲立之。

translations.literal: " At that time Altan and Quchar of the Emperor's clan were both at Ong Khan's side; the Emperor therefore sent Ariq to rebuke Ong Khan and also had him tell them, saying: "In former days our state had no lord; Kököchü and Daichu — two men who were in truth descendants of my grand-uncle Balaqa — were to be set up.
translations.idiomatic: " At that time Altan and Quchar of the Emperor's clan were both at Ong Khan's side. The Emperor sent Ariq to rebuke Ong Khan and also to tell them, "In former days our state had no lord. Kököchü and Daichu—descendants of my grand-uncle Balaqa—were to be set up as rulers.

sentences.zh: 二人既已固辭，乃以汝火察兒為伯父聶坤之子，又欲立之，汝又固辭。

translations.literal: When the two men had firmly declined, you Quchar, as son of your uncle Nekun, were next to be set up — and you too firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: When the two men firmly declined, you, Quchar, as son of your uncle Nekun, were next to be set up—and you too firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 然事不可中輟，復以汝按彈為我祖忽都剌之子，又欲立之，汝又固辭。

translations.literal: Yet the matter could not be left half-done; again you Altan, as son of my ancestor Qudu'ar, were to be set up — and you too firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the matter could not be left half-done. Again you, Altan, as son of my ancestor Qudu'ar, were to be set up—and you too firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 於是汝等推戴吾為之主，初豈我之本心哉，不自意相迫至於如此也。

translations.literal: Thereupon you pushed me forward and set me up as lord — this was never my original heart; I did not expect to be forced to this.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon you pushed me forward and set me up as lord. That was never my original wish; I did not expect to be forced to this.

sentences.zh: 三河，祖宗肇基之地，毋為他人所有。

translations.literal: The Three Rivers — the land where our forefathers first established the foundation — must not become another's possession.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Rivers—the land where our forefathers first laid the foundation—must not become another's possession.

sentences.zh: 汝善事汪罕，汪罕性無常，遇我尚如此，況汝輩乎？

translations.literal: Serve Ong Khan well; Ong Khan's nature is inconstant — toward me he has been thus, how much more toward you?
translations.idiomatic: Serve Ong Khan well. Ong Khan's nature is inconstant—toward me he has been thus; how much more toward you?

sentences.zh: 我今去矣，我今去矣！

translations.literal: I go now — I go now!
translations.idiomatic: I go now—I go now!

sentences.zh: 」按彈等無一言。

translations.literal: " Altan and the others did not speak a single word.
translations.idiomatic: " Altan and the others did not speak a single word.

sentences.zh: 帝既遣使於汪罕，遂進兵虜弘吉剌別部溺兒斤以行。

translations.literal: The Emperor, having sent envoys to Ong Khan, then advanced his army, captured the Hongirad sub-tribe of Nürjin, and marched on.
translations.idiomatic: After sending envoys to Ong Khan, the Emperor advanced his army, captured the Hongirad sub-tribe of Nürjin, and marched on.

sentences.zh: 至班硃尼河，河水方渾，帝飲之以誓眾。

translations.literal: When he reached the Baljuna River the water was still muddy; the Emperor drank of it to swear the host.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached the Baljuna River the water was still muddy. The Emperor drank of it to swear in the host.

sentences.zh: 有亦乞烈部人孛徒者，為火魯剌部所敗，因遇帝，與之同盟。

translations.literal: There was one Botu of the Ikires tribe, defeated by the Qorulas tribe; he met the Emperor on the way and entered alliance with him.
translations.idiomatic: Botu of the Ikires tribe, defeated by the Qorulas, met the Emperor on the way and entered alliance with him.

sentences.zh: 哈撒兒別居哈剌渾山，妻子為汪罕所虜，挾幼子脫虎走，糧絕，探鳥卵為食，來會於河上。

translations.literal: Khasar was living apart on Mount Qaraqun; his wife and children were captured by Ong Khan. Clutching his young son Toqu he fled; when provisions ran out he dug up birds' eggs for food, and came to join the Emperor on the river.
translations.idiomatic: Khasar was living apart on Mount Qaraqun. Ong Khan captured his wife and children; clutching his young son Toqu, Khasar fled. When provisions ran out he dug up birds' eggs for food and came to join the Emperor on the river.

sentences.zh: 時汪罕形勢盛強，帝微弱，勝敗未可知，眾頗危懼。

translations.literal: At that time Ong Khan's position was strong and flourishing while the Emperor was weak; victory or defeat could not be known, and many were deeply afraid.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Ong Khan's position was strong while the Emperor was weak. Victory or defeat could not be known, and many were deeply afraid.

sentences.zh: 凡與飲河水者，謂之飲渾水，言其曾同艱難也。

translations.literal: All who drank the river water were called drinkers of muddy water — meaning that they had once shared hardship together.
translations.idiomatic: All who drank the river water were called drinkers of muddy water—meaning they had once shared hardship together.

sentences.zh: 汪罕兵至，帝與戰於哈闌真沙陀之地，汪罕大敗，其臣按彈、火察兒、劄木合等謀弑汪罕，弗克，往奔乃蠻。

translations.literal: Ong Khan's army arrived; the Emperor fought him at Qaradan Jalatu. Ong Khan was utterly defeated. His ministers Altan, Quchar, Jamuqa, and others plotted to assassinate Ong Khan but could not succeed, and fled to the Naiman.
translations.idiomatic: When Ong Khan's army arrived, the Emperor fought him at Qaradan Jalatu and put him to utter rout. Altan, Quchar, Jamuqa, and other ministers plotted to assassinate Ong Khan but failed, and fled to the Naiman.

sentences.zh: 答力台、把憐等部稽顙來降。

translations.literal: The tribes of Targhutai and Balin came forward with bowed foreheads to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: The tribes of Targhutai and Balin came forward with bowed foreheads to surrender.

sentences.zh: 帝移軍斡難河源，謀攻汪罕，復遣二使往汪罕，偽為哈撒兒之言曰：「我兄太子今既不知所在，我之妻孥又在王所，縱我欲往，將安所之耶？

translations.literal: The Emperor moved his army to the source of the Onon River, planned to attack Ong Khan, and again sent two envoys to Ong Khan, feigning Khasar's words, saying: "My elder brother the Prince — I do not know where he is now; my wife and children are again in Your Majesty's hands. Even if I wished to go to him, where could I go?
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor moved his army to the source of the Onon River and planned to attack Ong Khan. He again sent two envoys to Ong Khan, feigning Khasar's words: "My elder brother the Prince—I do not know where he is now, and my wife and children are again in Your Majesty's hands. Even if I wished to go to him, where could I go?

sentences.zh: 王儻棄我前愆，念我舊好，即束手來歸矣。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty will put aside my former fault and remember our old friendship, I shall come with bound hands to submit.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty will put aside my former fault and remember our old friendship, I shall come with bound hands to submit.

sentences.zh: 」汪罕信之，因遣人隨二使來，以皮囊盛血與之盟。

translations.literal: " Ong Khan believed it; he therefore sent men to follow the two envoys, and they swore alliance with blood in a leather bag.
translations.idiomatic: " Ong Khan believed it. He sent men to follow the two envoys, and they swore alliance with blood in a leather bag.

sentences.zh: 及至，即以二使為嚮導，令軍士銜枚夜趨折折運都山，出其不意，襲汪罕，敗之，盡降克烈部眾，汪罕與亦剌合挺身遁去。

translations.literal: When they arrived, he used the two envoys as guides, had the soldiers take twigs in their mouths, and by night hurried toward Mount Jeje'ün; catching Ong Khan unawares, he attacked and defeated him, fully subduing the Kerait tribesmen. Ong Khan and Ilugei escaped alone.
translations.idiomatic: When they arrived, he used the two envoys as guides, had the soldiers take twigs in their mouths, and by night hurried toward Mount Jeje'ün. Catching Ong Khan unawares, he attacked and defeated him and fully subdued the Kerait tribesmen. Ong Khan and Ilugei escaped alone.

sentences.zh: 汪罕歎曰：「我為吾兒所誤，今日之禍，悔將何及！

translations.literal: Ong Khan sighed and said: "I was misled by my son — today's disaster: what regret can still avail!
translations.idiomatic: Ong Khan sighed and said, "I was misled by my son—today's disaster: what regret can still avail!

sentences.zh: 」汪罕出走，路逢乃蠻部將，遂為其所殺。

translations.literal: " Ong Khan fled; on the road he met a Naiman tribal commander and was killed by him.
translations.idiomatic: " Ong Khan fled. On the road he met a Naiman tribal commander and was killed by him.

sentences.zh: 亦剌哈走西夏，日剽掠以自資。

translations.literal: Ilugei fled to the Western Xia and daily raided to support himself.
translations.idiomatic: Ilugei fled to the Western Xia and daily raided to support himself.
